summary: Summation No. 21 covers USAMGIK activities in South Korea for June 1947, with economic statistics mostly for April and May. The Korean Interim Legislative Assembly ended its long franchise-law dispute on 27 June, setting the minimum voting age at 23 after Speaker Kimm Kiu Sic's resignation threat. The U.S.-U.S.S.R. Joint Commission issued Communique No. 11, circulated questionnaires on the provisional government's charter and platform to parties, and moved to Pyongyang for consultations. Rightist ranks split over participation. Economic sections report record April coal output, record salt output, rising Bank of Chosen note circulation, the new Korean Foreign Exchange Bank, a revised income tax law, rail and power figures, and grain-import tables. Social sections cover cholera immunization, refugees from the North (102,185 since January), repatriation, textbooks, school statistics, the National Youth Movement and press reaction. The volume is a Digitized-by-Google University of Virginia copy, useful to historians for the Joint Commission texts and detailed statistics.
highlights: The Interim Legislative Assembly passed the General Franchise Law on 27 June with a compromise minimum voting age of 23 (40 votes to 26 for 21), after Speaker Kimm Kiu Sic and Vice-speakers Choe Tong O and Yun Ki Sop resigned over a 25-year requirement and withdrew on 9 June.

Joint Communique No. 11 (12 June) set the method of consulting Korean parties; 344 parties had obtained copies by 19 June, applications were due 23 June, answers extended from 1 July to 5 July, and the delegations left for Pyongyang on 25-26 June.

The Hankuk Democratic Party decided to join Joint Commission deliberations, splitting the Rightists led by Syngman Rhee and Kim Koo, while the South Korea Labor Party named Pak Hun Tung its representative and demanded Rhee and Kim be expelled.

April coal production reached 31,318 metric tons, the highest since liberation but 4,182 tons short of the 35,500-ton quota; anthracite supplies of 35,305 tons met only part of the 85,000-ton requirement.

Bank of Chosen notes in circulation rose by 617,893,769 yen to 18,035,603,028 yen on 30 June; government revenues rose 22.4 percent in May to 1,022,599,160 yen against expenditures of 1,177,290,509 yen.

An ordinance of 16 June created the Korean Foreign Exchange Bank, capitalized at 500,000,000 yen with the Interim Government subscribing 200,000,000; the revised Third Income Tax Law took effect 21 June with rates of 3 to 90 percent.
Refugee movement from North Korea totaled 24,501 in June (102,185 for 1947 to 28 June); seven 38th-parallel camps cared for 74,637 persons and 9,092 refugee housing units were complete by 30 June.

A Pusan stevedore strike began 28 May and was settled through conciliation with wage increases under the Wage Rate and Incentive Board plan; salt production hit a postwar high of 32,207 metric tons in May.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Library covers, title pages for Summation No. 21 (June 1947), table of contents and list of charts, maps and graphs.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Overview of June 1947: the franchise law, Joint Commission consultations, coal and finance news, health, refugees, education and public information.

sections.title: Section 1. Political Activities
sections.summary: Speaker Kimm's resignation threat and the 27 June franchise law (voting age 23), the Rightist split, Joint Commission Communique No. 11 with 344 parties applying, and the 25 June move to Pyongyang.

sections.title: Section 2. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Rice transplanting of 2,824,466 acres, April coal at 31,318 tons, salt at 32,207 tons, the new Foreign Exchange Bank, note circulation of 18,035,603,028 yen, and summer-grain prices.

sections.title: Section 3. Social Activities
sections.summary: Cholera immunization, 4,863 renewed doctors, 102,185 refugees from the North, 9,129,922 textbooks distributed, the youth movement, and a poll favoring a 20-year voting age.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Franchise law and Joint Commission documents, plus legal and public safety matters: police, prisons and fires.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Assembly resignations and the 23-year voting-age compromise, Rightist and Leftist maneuvering, full text of Joint Communique No. 11, Decisions 5 and 6 questionnaires, and the 25 June Seoul meeting.

sections.title: Section 2. Legal and Public Safety
sections.summary: Orderly Rightist demonstration of 23 June, 80 percent of police lacking pre-liberation experience, 20,554 prisoners in May, 92 fires, and Constabulary training courses.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Coal, salt, silk, currency, trade, railroads, power, communications and price statistics, including record April coal and the Foreign Exchange Bank.

sections.title: Section 1. Natural Resources
sections.summary: Rice transplanting, New Korea Company operating 661,000 acres, February fish landings of 25,027 tons, Kyonggi-do forest erosion, and April coal output of 31,318 tons.

sections.title: Section 2. Industry
sections.summary: Flour, noodle, salt, paper and brick output, a silk ceiling price of 54.40 yen, cotton and silk cloth production, and the Pusan stevedore strike settlement.

sections.title: Section 3. Commerce
sections.summary: Note circulation of 18.0 billion yen, the Foreign Exchange Bank, revised income tax, vested property sales, May import jump, rail and power data, public works spending of 362,831,452 yen.

sections.title: Section 4. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Basic rice ration of about 0.23 pound, summer-grain purchase prices (wheat 1,792 yen per suk), 46 percent of fertilizer sold, petroleum distribution down 24 percent, falling April free-market prices.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Refugee relief, school statistics and press commentary on the Joint Commission, within public health, education, culture, religion and public information.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: Cholera immunization, 348 veterinarians, 7,840 lepers, flood-relief and low-cost feeding programs, 24,501 June refugees, 9,092 refugee houses and 1,691 Koreans repatriated.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Culture and Religion
sections.summary: Seoul National University morale, school financing survey, 9,129,922 textbooks, 442,979 library volumes, National Youth Movement at 150,000 members, Boy Scout handbook and Oslo delegates.

sections.title: Section 3. Public Information
sections.summary: 600,000 leaflets dropped on Joint Commission news, 35 films reviewed, radio weather forecasts, a suffrage-age poll of 1,149 persons, and press reaction to the Rightist division over cooperation.

sections.title: Map of Korea
sections.summary: Fold-out map of Korea listed in the charts, maps and graphs index.

sections.title: Back matter
sections.summary: University of Virginia library due-date slip, blank pages, barcode page and back cover of the digitized copy.
